title: Five-host re-verification of the routing matrix's lever facts against the atlas lever cells

checks.quotes_found_in_cited_evidence: 39 of 42 verbatim after ignoring markup; the other 3 differ only by a markdown link target or an ellipsis

rows.fact: Claude tier map: fast claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, balanced claude-sonnet-5, top claude-opus-4-8
rows.quote: Without ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL, the opus alias on Amazon Bedrock resolves to Opus 5.5, and without ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL, the sonnet alias resolves to Sonnet 4.5.
rows.note: Newer Opus is the alias target (the quote covers Bedrock only). The full ids are pinned, so they may still work; the first-party default is not quoted.

rows.fact: Current Claude opus id is claude-opus-4-8 and fable is claude-fable-5
rows.quote: Without ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL, the opus alias on Amazon Bedrock resolves to Opus 5.5
rows.note: Bedrock-scoped quote. The sibling capability map already calls Opus 4.8 and Fable 5 Legacy.

rows.fact: Claude Code has a native effort dial for non-default effort
rows.quote: --effort | Set the effort level for the current session. Options: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, or ultracode.
rows.note: Also the /effort selector slider (E-claude-code-00122).

rows.fact: Dynamic Workflows in Claude Code orchestrate hundreds of parallel subagents
rows.quote: Runs a dynamic workflow: a script that orchestrates many subagents in the background and returns one consolidated result.
rows.note: A run is capped at 1,000 agents (E-claude-code-15872).
rows.reviewer_caveat: holds for orchestration of many subagents; the atlas states a 1,000-agent cap per run, not a parallel count

rows.fact: Opus 5 effort defaults to high in Claude Code
rows.note: Atlas quotes only a Projects default ('a new project runs every thread on Opus at high effort') without naming Opus 5. Per-model session defaults are not quoted.

rows.fact: Raising the Codex reasoning level costs latency, not dollars
rows.quote: Higher reasoning effort increases response time and token usage, but it can improve quality for complex work.
rows.note: More tokens cost more. Line 48 ('latency only') says the same thing. Line 37 ('no change in per-token cost') is not contradicted.

rows.fact: Codex tier map: fast gpt-5.6-luna, balanced gpt-5.6-terra, top gpt-5.6-sol
rows.quote: /model | Choose the active model (and reasoning effort, when available). | Use gpt-6-luna or gpt-6.1-sol if shown.
rows.note: Codex docs now point to gpt-6-luna and gpt-6.1-sol. There is no Terra tier in the quote.

rows.fact: Codex pro is a reasoning mode on Sol, not a separate slug
rows.quote: Reasoning effort advertised by the selected model, such as low, medium, high, xhigh, max, or ultra.
rows.note: Atlas gives Sol's effort as Light to Ultra and never names a pro mode. It is possibly renamed; treat it as unconfirmed.

rows.fact: Codex balanced default is GPT-6 Sol
rows.quote: Use gpt-6-luna or gpt-6.1-sol if shown.
rows.note: Docs name gpt-6.1-sol, not GPT-6 Sol, so the model was renamed or bumped.

rows.fact: Codex cheapest fast tier is GPT-6 Luna
rows.quote: Use gpt-6-luna or gpt-6.1-sol if shown.
rows.note: The quote confirms the model is offered. That it is the cheapest is pricing and was not checked.
rows.reviewer_caveat: holds only that the model exists; the pricing claim was not checked

rows.fact: Codex /model switches both the model and its reasoning level
rows.quote: /model | Choose the active model (and reasoning effort, when available).
rows.note: It sets effort only when the model supports it.

rows.fact: Reasoning level on Codex is a dial on the same model, separate from changing the model
rows.quote: /reasoning | Choose the reasoning effort for the current chat.
rows.note: Also config model_reasoning_effort. The cost advice is not covered.

rows.fact: Effort override on Codex CLI goes through an --effort flag (named with cheap-lane's flag)
rows.note: Atlas puts effort in config model_reasoning_effort, /reasoning, the app control and the GitHub action. Only Codex Security CLI has --effort. cheap-lane has no codex agent.

rows.fact: Codex long-run agent and top tier is GPT-6 Astra
rows.note: No cited quote names Astra. The catalog cell describes discovery (model/list, codex debug models), not a model list.

rows.fact: Copilot CLI's only confirmed-working --model value is auto; six pinned slugs (incl. claude-haiku-4.5) were rejected at the API level
rows.quote: --model=MODEL | Choose the AI model (for example, gpt-5.4 or claude-haiku-4.5). Useful for pinning a model in reproducible workflows.
rows.note: Docs document pinning by slug. The file's rejections were a v0.305.0 probe; enterprise model enablement (E-copilot-cli-00353) could explain them, so re-probe.

rows.fact: Copilot --effort choices are none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max
rows.quote: Set the reasoning effort level (low, medium, high, xhigh, max).
rows.note: The docs list five values, without none or minimal. The settings effortLevel accepts low..xhigh, default medium (E-copilot-cli-03753).

rows.fact: Copilot CLI takes an --effort flag for non-default effort
rows.quote: --effort=LEVEL, --reasoning-effort=LEVEL | Set the reasoning effort level (low, medium, high, xhigh, max).
rows.note: The sentence refers to cheap-lane's wrapper flag. The host flag exists.

rows.fact: Copilot Auto has named tiers efficiency / balance / intelligence, available in Copilot CLI
rows.quote: Use /model auto TIER (efficiency, balance, or intelligence) to select a specific Auto routing tier directly
rows.note: The file marks this [verify-at-use].

rows.fact: Copilot CLI has task-based auto model selection (Auto routes by task)
rows.quote: Auto intelligently chooses models based on real-time system health and model performance ... and the complexity of the task you have given Copilot.

rows.fact: Copilot model availability varies by plan and org policy; admins must enable models
rows.quote: Users can only access AI models that are enabled at the enterprise level.
rows.note: The five-vendor picker claim in the same sentence is not covered.

rows.fact: Copilot tier models as display names: Claude Haiku 4.5, Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Opus 5
rows.note: Atlas lists no Copilot model set. Its --model examples are slugs (claude-haiku-4.5), not the display names this map uses.

rows.fact: Copilot CLI offers Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, Grok 4.6 and others as of 2026-09
rows.note: Atlas has no model list for Copilot, only example slugs (gpt-5.4, claude-haiku-4.5).

rows.fact: Copilot --model auto rejects --effort; effort applies only with a pinned effort-capable model
rows.note: Atlas says only that some models support reasoning levels. It does not address Auto combined with --effort.

rows.fact: No valid pinned Copilot --model slug is discoverable non-interactively
rows.note: Atlas cites a Supported AI models docs page and example slugs, and lists available models via /model. Non-interactive enumeration is not addressed.

rows.fact: Models are selectable in VS Code across all modes: chat / ask / edit / agent
rows.quote: Which instructions, tools, and behavior apply to a task. Examples include Agent, Plan, Ask, and custom agents.
rows.note: The atlas lists the roles as Agent, Plan, Ask and custom. There is no Edit mode, and Plan is new.

rows.fact: Copilot Chat's chat-mode surface is 'Copilot Chat / edit'
rows.quote: Examples include Agent, Plan, Ask, and custom agents.
rows.note: No Edit mode is named. The supervised read/answer role is now Ask (no edits) or Plan.

rows.fact: VS Code Copilot Chat exposes an interactive model picker directly
rows.quote: Use the language model picker in the chat input field to change the model for chat conversations and code editing.
rows.note: The file calls it the /model picker; the atlas describes a picker in the chat input field, not a /model command.

rows.fact: Copilot Auto routing tiers roll out in VS Code
rows.quote: When the default model is Auto, set the autoTier Copilot managed setting to choose how new chats initially optimize model routing
rows.note: VS Code has an autoTier setting. The three tier names are quoted only from the CLI docs.

rows.fact: Copilot offers Auto; let it pick the model unless you have a reason to override
rows.quote: With auto model selection, VS Code evaluates task complexity and real-time model availability to route each request to the optimal model.
rows.note: The when-to-override advice is editorial and was not checked.

rows.fact: Enterprise admins can set model=auto as the default for new conversations
rows.quote: Sets the default chat model for new conversations. Accepts 'auto', a model family name (such as 'opus' or 'gemini'), or a full model id.
rows.note: The policy is chat.defaultModel and needs VS Code 1.127 or later.

rows.fact: GitHub tracks Copilot model availability per client (VS Code, Copilot CLI), not per Chat vs CLI, so both resolve through one copilot row
rows.note: Catalog cells say availability depends on harness, account and policy; neither mentions a per-client availability table.

rows.fact: Copilot top tier is Claude Opus 5.5 and the balanced default is Claude Sonnet 5
rows.note: Atlas names no specific Copilot models in VS Code.

rows.fact: Grok tier map: fast and balanced use grok-4.5, top uses grok-4.6
rows.quote: grok-4.7, SpaceXAI's latest model, is available directly on the xAI API.
rows.note: Atlas names grok-4.7 as the latest model. It does not mention 4.5 or 4.6 or say they are gone.

rows.fact: Each Grok Build sub-agent runs in an isolated Git worktree/branch
rows.quote: Subagents can also request worktree isolation when the parent delegates parallel work.
rows.note: Worktree isolation is opt-in per request, not automatic. GROK_SUBAGENTS also defaults to 0 (E-grok-build-00066).

rows.fact: Grok CLI --effort accepts low|medium|high and rejects xhigh
rows.quote: Reasoning efforts (supported): low, medium, high, xhigh
rows.note: xhigh is supported on Grok 4.7. The rejection was probed against the 4.5/4.6 tier models, which have no documented levels.

rows.fact: Grok 4.7 is the current Grok flagship, superseding 4.6, and is used in Grok Build
rows.quote: grok-4.7, SpaceXAI's latest model, is available directly on the xAI API. Drop it into your own agent loop, IDE integration, or coding tool.
rows.note: Latest-model holds. The quote is from the Grok Build overview page but speaks of the API; Grok Build CLI availability is not stated directly.
rows.reviewer_caveat: holds for the latest-model claim; the quote is about the xAI API and does not state Grok Build CLI availability

rows.fact: Grok Build has a plan mode
rows.quote: Only the session plan file may be edited until you approve. Other edit tools are rejected, including under auto or always-approve.
rows.note: The file's 'sub-task graph in a TUI' detail is not quoted. Plan mode gates edit tools, not the shell.

rows.fact: Grok effort per tier: fast=low, balanced/top=high on grok-4.5/grok-4.6
rows.note: Atlas lists effort levels for Grok 4.7 only (low, medium, high, xhigh). It gives none for 4.5 or 4.6.

rows.fact: Grok 4.6 is the balanced/mid Grok option and still selectable
rows.note: Atlas names only grok-4.7.

rows.fact: Grok 4.6 is the Grok Build CLI default model; 4.5 remains selectable (2026-08-14)
rows.note: Atlas documents GROK_DEFAULT_MODEL and -m but gives no default value.

rows.fact: grok-build-0.1, grok-build, grok-4.3 and grok-4.20 are unknown model ids in the Grok Build CLI
rows.note: Atlas does not list rejected ids.

rows.fact: Grok Build runs up to 8 parallel sub-agents
rows.note: The concurrency cell quotes only a 50 scheduled-task cap, and total-agent-caps is undocumented.
